Simulate analytically normalised trajectories on independent segments

Source: R/simulate.R
simulate_ssf.Rd

Supports the canonical gamma kernel and the step-length families of fit_ssf(). With an explicit family, use a fitted exact kernel, with optional persistence and a single prospective target direction. No finite control-point approximation is used for simulation. With a target effect, the nearest supplied fixed target is recomputed at the current position before each step. Movement is unbounded; neither the raster extent nor observed positions are imposed as barriers. With lag_log_step, the first step has no AR adjustment. Later steps use the previous simulated length within the same segment. Daily lags from 22 to 26 hours use earlier simulated lengths within the same segment. Hourly effects on the gamma mean apply from the first step.

Usage

simulate_ssf(
  fit,
  segments,
  n_sims = 1L,
  target_points = NULL,
  state_path = NULL,
  target_term = "cos_diff_theta_to_target",
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

fit

An ssf_fit with an explicit density measure and valid kernels.

segments

Data frame with unique ID, x, y, bearing and n_steps columns. These give starting positions, previous headings, and step counts. With daily transitions, include hour (0 to 23) for each segment's first step origin. The simulator advances one hour per step.

n_sims

Number of independent simulated replicates.

target_points

Optional finite two-column matrix of fixed target points. Required if a target coefficient is nonzero. Nearest-target queries use an exact internal two-dimensional tree. At zero target distance its directional effect is set to zero.

state_path

Optional fixed integer state path for all segments. NULL simulates a new Markov path, restarting from stationarity at each segment. A fixed path gives a conditional diagnostic, not a full generative check.

target_term

Name of the single directional target coefficient.

seed

Optional seed; the previous RNG state is restored on exit.

Value

An ssf_simulations list with tracks, segment metadata, method and seed. Track rows are generated endpoints, not the initial positions. Parameters remain fixed; parameter uncertainty is not propagated.
